reason: The text explicitly describes the systematic oppression of the Hebrew people (בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל). After a new Egyptian Pharaoh rises who has no knowledge of Joseph and fears the Hebrews' numerical strength, he implements oppressive measures: placing taskmasters (שָׂרֵי מִסִּים) over them 'to afflict them' (לְמַעַן עַנֹּתוֹ) with heavy burdens (בְּסִבְלֹתָם), and forcing them into forced labor to build treasure cities (Pithom and Raamses). The verb יְעַנּוּ ('they afflicted') is used repeatedly to describe their treatment. The passage establishes the beginning of Hebrew bondage and persecution in Egypt—a foundational oppression narrative.
